newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN COMPLAINTS OVER PHONE SERVICE ON THE RISE.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN COMPLAINTS OVER PHONE SERVICE ON THE RISE.

text.p: With the liberalisation of the European telecommunications market just eight months away, Belgians are increasingly complaining about services provided by state telephone company Belgacom.

"Belgacom still has a few months to brace for competition. We wish them success in doing so," telecommunications ombudsman Edgard Vandebosch told a news conference on the ombudsman's 1996 annual report.
The total number of complaints more than doubled to 4,459 from 2,155 in 1995, with Belgacom accounting for nearly 88 percent.
The remainder was related mainly to Belgacom Directory Services (BDS) which publishes phone directories, and GSM operator Belgacom Mobile with 2.4 and 3.6 percent respectively.
Mobistar, which has been operating the country's second mobile phone network since late August 1996, accounted for 1.4 percent.
Nearly a third of all complaints -- 1,453 -- were related to phone bills against 982 in 1995. The number of complaints linked to phone connections jumped to 422 from 92 in 1995.
The number of complaints about phone directories more than doubled to 417.
"If two books about the same subject are issued, the chance that mistakes are made also doubles," Vandebosch said.
Both BDS and rival company ITT-Promedia, a unit of U.S.-based ITT Corp produce guides. BDS is 80 percent owned by Belgacom and 20 percent by GTE-Directories, a unit of U.S.-based GTE Corp .
Belgacom is owned 49.9 percent by a consortium comprising Ameritech , Singapore Telecom , TeleDanmark and three Belgian investors.
